entries.test: Archived launch-period AI search summaries would show whether they supplied dangerously harmful advice alongside conspicuously absurd answers.
entries.note: The evaluative adjectives accompany a concrete claim about documented outputs.

entries.test: Google's quarterly financial reports and dated AI announcements would establish whether its intensified AI push followed near-zero nominal growth and negative inflation-adjusted growth in Q4 2022.
entries.note: The passage establishes temporal sequence, without explicitly claiming that the quarter caused the AI push. 'Desperate' is editorial characterization.

entries.test: Google's reported 2024 capital expenditures, infrastructure spending disclosures, and 2019–2023 expenditures would settle the numerical spending claim.
entries.note: The normalization turns 'essentially killed its golden goose' into an unqualified claim that Google killed search. The spending component is independently testable.

entries.test: Contemporaneous recordings, screenshots, and Google's acknowledgments would establish whether its search summaries recommended eating rocks and putting glue on pizza.
entries.note: The source describes public reactions and how Google's innovation 'seemed'; the normalization adds an unqualified conclusion that the summaries made search worse.
The inference about Google's direction is Zitron's own, although the supporting description of Fox is Pichai's. 'Going all-in' supplies no shared threshold for Google's degree of commitment.

entries.test: Contemporaneous developer discussions, surveys, and published accounts would show complaints about model usefulness, marketing, and integration into Google products.
entries.note: This is Zitron's assertion, outside the quotation attributed to Pichai. It does not explicitly claim that every developer holds these views.
He explicitly labels this a hypothesis and says 'likely'; the elapsed date does not make it a firm prediction.
The normalization preserves the explicit 'likely' hedge.
'More than likely' remains probability language about Google's present strategic view.
'Signals' strengthens the source's 'suggests.' Neither 'disarray' nor improvement 'in a hurry' supplies a shared evidentiary threshold.
The slow-collapse language is a broad metaphor, with no specified business outcome.

entries.test: Product launch histories and adoption or revenue evidence, together with public transaction records and reporting on the $2.7 billion arrangement, would test the product and acquisition assertions.
entries.note: 'Most meaningful acquisition' does not mean 'biggest recent deal.' Commercially significant new products provide a plain test of the sweeping product claim.

entries.test: Public evidence of sustained mainstream uses and disclosed inference costs and revenues would test the utility and per-prompt economics assertions.
entries.note: 'Burns cash with every prompt' asserts expenditure without necessarily asserting a net loss on every prompt. The normalization makes the financial claim more specific.

entries.test: Contemporaneous market growth data and public investment opportunities would show whether rapidly expanding markets besides generative AI remained available to Google at multibillion-dollar scale.
entries.note: This is a sweeping factual claim about available markets, despite its polemical framing.
